title: session-pulse latency vs cost snapshot - draft
content:
Purpose
This is a working draft of a short benchmark snapshot comparing sessionized request patterns against steady-state throughput for three run profiles (interactive, mixed, bulk). The goal is to give product and SRE teams a compact view of where latency and per-query cost diverge when we enable different runtime knobs (KV cache on/off, smallbatch vs dynamic batch, and quantization profile Q2/Q4).

Key takeaways (TL;DR)
- KV cache dramatically reduces p50 and per-query cost for conversational session workloads with repeated prefixes; median cost reduction ~32%, p95 latency improves by 18% for 8-turn sessions.
- Smallbatch (fixed slot sizes) is best for strict p99 SLOs at low concurrency; dynamic-batching wins for cost at higher concurrency but increases p99 tail by ~40–90ms depending on model length.
- Q4 quant (aggressive) reduces GPU-side token time by ~22% on A100-like instances but increases decode CPU overhead; net cost win depends on throughput mix.

Methodology (short)
- Synthetic session generator that replays 10k sessions per profile over 1 hour runs. Session length distributions: interactive (1–6 turns, median 3), mixed (1–20, median 7), bulk (1–120, median 35).
- Models: llama-2-13b-serve (baseline), llama-2-13b-q4 (quant), rlnet-7b (lighter) — these are shorthand tags for the catalog entries used in the runs.
- Hardware: n1-gpu-a100-40GB-equivalent (single-GPU workers).
- Knobs varied: KV cache ON/OFF, batcher mode smallbatch/dynbatch, prewarm pool size 0/4, concurrency per-worker 1/8.
- Metrics collected: p50/p95/p99 latency (ms), tokens/sec per-GPU, amortized $/query (platform internal cost model).

Compact results (representative sample rows)
Profile | Model | Cache | Batcher | p50 (ms) | p95 (ms) | p99 (ms) | tks/sec/GPU | $/query
------- | ----- | ----- | ------- | -------- | ------- | ------- | ---------- | ------
interactive | llama-13b | ON | smallbatch | 78 | 165 | 230 | 320 | $0.0042
interactive | llama-13b | OFF | smallbatch | 112 | 218 | 315 | 290 | $0.0061
interactive | llama-13b-q4 | ON | dynbatch | 92 | 189 | 310 | 380 | $0.0035
mixed | llama-13b | ON | dynbatch | 165 | 420 | 680 | 420 | $0.0056
mixed | rlnet-7b | ON | dynbatch | 110 | 270 | 410 | 740 | $0.0031
bulk | llama-13b | OFF | dynbatch | 340 | 920 | 1450 | 980 | $0.0022

Observations from the numbers
- Interactive sessions: turning cache ON yields the biggest latency improvement for p50/p95 because repeated prefix tokens avoid recomputation; cost correlates strongly with p50 here because many sessions are short.
- Mixed profile: dynbatch increases throughput (tks/sec/GPU) which reduces $/query relative to smallbatch at scale, but p99 suffers moderately. This is the classic throughput vs tail tradeoff.
- Bulk workloads: amortized cost is lowest (due to long context amortization), but tail latency climbs sharply, implying different SLOs required for long-running analyses.

Simple ASCII visualizations (for quick skimming)
Per-query cost by profile (lower is better):
interactive : ██████████  ($0.0048 avg)
mixed       : ███████████████  ($0.0049 avg)
bulk        : █████████████████████  ($0.0023 avg)

p99 latency (ms) by profile (higher is worse):
interactive : ███████ (230)
mixed       : █████████████ (680)
bulk        : ███████████████████████ (1450)

Operational implications
- For PLG-hosted API: recommend defaulting interactive traffic to smallbatch with KV cache ON and conservative prewarm (pool 2–4) to protect p99s while keeping $/query modest.
- For Dedicated customers with strict p50/p95: offer a 'latency-first' preset (smallbatch + no-aggressive-quant + prewarm=4) and a separate 'cost-savings' preset (dynbatch + q4 optional) with clear guidance on tail tradeoffs.
- For Private/on-prem: add an automated tuning job that sweeps batcher mode and cache TTLs over a 24–72 hour traffic replay and recommends a rollout.

Open questions / unknowns (todo)
- Interaction of aggressive quant (Q4) with KV cache hit patterns — does quant error change auto-caching benefits? Need a separate A/B that measures quality drift for mix-sensitive prompts.
- CPU decode bottleneck in q4 cases: for low-token-latency workloads, cpu cost starts to dominate; measure actual host-level $ delta.
- Multi-GPU tiling: how do session affinity policies change the amortization curves? Run a short 4-GPU tiling sweep.

Suggested next experiments (short list)
- 24h replay of production traces for a high-variance tenant using: {cache ON/OFF} x {smallbatch/dynbatch} x {q2/q4} and capture decode-CPU cost.
- Focused p99 exercise: hold throughput fixed, vary worker-concurrency and prewarm size to quantify tail improvements per-$ spent.
- Quality check: sample 5k responses from q4 variant for mixed profile, run automated evals (toxicity, coherence regression) and human spot checks.

Appendix: raw run config sample (shorthand)
- run_id: session-pulse-2029-01-11-a
- model: llama-13b
- hw: a100-40gb-sim
- sessions: 10k (mixed)
- batcher: dynbatch (max_slot=16, slot_timeout=15ms)
- kv_cache: enabled (ttl=300s)
- prewarm_pool: 2
- concurrency: per_worker=8

Notes for reviewers
- This is an internal snapshot intended for product & SRE planning; results are sensitive to the synthetic generator distribution and cost model assumptions. Please flag any requests for deeper breakdowns (per-route, per-token-length slices, or tenant-specific runs).
- If we want to present this externally, we should collapse into a 1-page infographic and remove internal cost model fields.

End of draft
